claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you asking about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes thanks - I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So you're asking about your son Alex who is 11 years old.

Now, to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

**Do you live with Alex, or if he lives elsewhere, do you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum. But I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep each week for things like clothes and other bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about the financial contributions you make.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week, and is anyone else (such as his mum) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I pay £26.05 a week towards his upkeep. As far as I know, his mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. That's helpful information.

Just to clarify one important point: **Are you certain that Alex's mum is not claiming Child Benefit for him, or is it that you're not sure whether she's claiming it?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm certain - his mum isn't claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation provided by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually - Alex has been in hospital for a while now, about 15 weeks or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. This is an important detail that affects eligibility.

**During the time Alex has been in hospital, have you been regularly spending money on him (for example, buying things for him, providing pocket money, or other expenses)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure to be honest. I mean, it's been quite difficult with him being in there for so long. I'd have to think about whether I've been able to keep up with buying things for him regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it's a difficult situation and I appreciate your honesty.

Let me ask one final question to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex in a hospital here in the UK, or is he in a hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's in a hospital here in the UK.

**Your situation involves several factors:**

1. **Positive factors:** Alex is 11 years old (under 16), you live in the UK, and you contribute £26.05 per week towards his upkeep, which shows financial responsibility for him. His mother is not claiming Child Benefit for him.

2. **Complicating factors:** Alex has been in hospital for approximately 15 weeks. Under the Child Benefit rules, after a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, entitlement usually ends. However, there is an important exception - you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child in a UK hospital if you regularly spend money on them.

3. **The key uncertainty:** You've mentioned that you're not sure whether you've been regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay. This is the crucial piece of information needed to determine if the exception applies to your case.

**What this means:** Without being able to confirm whether you've been regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay, I cannot definitively say whether you would be eligible or not.

If you can clarify whether you have been regularly buying things for Alex or providing him with money during his time in hospital, please contact the Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific circumstances. They can help assess whether you qualify under the exception to the 12-week rule.
